title: Amul Business Model: Do Farmers Get ₹80 of ₹100?
description:
How does Amul's business model work? Amul is a cooperative owned by about 3.6 million dairy farmers in Gujarat, India. Amul says farmers get about ₹80-85 of every ₹100 a shopper spends on its products, compared with about a third in many other countries (Amul's own claim from GCMMF annual general meeting speeches, not an independent audit; the one-third comparison is from Jayen Mehta via Rural Voice). That leaves little for everything else, yet the Amul brand topped ₹1 lakh crore (₹1 trillion, about $10.7 billion) in sales in FY2025-26, on about 31 million litres of milk a day. The lesson: a thin margin on huge volume can build a giant.

How it works: village dairy cooperatives collect the milk, 18 district unions process it, and the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF) sells it under the Amul brand. GCMMF's own sales were ₹73,450 crore; the brand figure also includes the district unions.

Sources: GCMMF FY2025-26 results (5 Apr 2026, via DeshGujarat and Dairy Industries International); Jayen Mehta, GCMMF, quoted by Rural Voice (25 Jun 2022); GCMMF chairman's address, 50th Annual General Body Meeting (amul.com); Amul, 'The Amul Model' and 'A note on the achievements of the dairy cooperatives' (amul.com). Dollar figure at ₹93.44 per $ (PTI, 18 Nov 2026). 1 crore = 10 million; 1 lakh crore = 1 trillion.

visual.label: of every ₹100 goes to farmers (Amul's claim)

scenes.say: Ah-mool's Jayen Mayta says elsewhere, farmers often get about a third.
Because farmers own it. Three point six million of them.
Villages collect the milk, eighteen district unions process it, one federation sells it.
Now the twist: that leaves at most twenty rupees for everything else, shops included.
Yet Ah-mool brand sales topped one lakh crore rupees: over ten billion dollars.
That's from thirty-one million litres of milk, every single day.
The lesson: thin margins on huge volume can build a giant.
So next time you buy a packet of milk, remember...
